'''Theodore William Chaundy''' (19 January 1889 – 14 April 1966) was an English [[mathematician]] who introduced [[Burchnall–Chaundy theory]].

Chaundy was born to widowed businessman John Chaundy and his second wife Sarah Pates in their shop-cum-home at 49 [[Broad Street, Oxford|Broad Street]] in [[Oxford]]. John had eight children, one of whom died as a toddler, with his late first wife and died barely a year after Chaundy was born. The Chaundy home along Broad Street has since been demolished.<ref name="Chaundy">{{cite web|title=Burials: John & Maria Chaundy|url=http://www.stsepulchres.org.uk/burials/chaundy_john.html|publisher=[[St Sepulchre's Cemetery]]}}</ref>

Chaundy attended [[Oxford High School for Boys]] and read mathematics at [[Balliol College, Oxford]] on a scholarship. In 1912 he became a lecturer at Oxford and later named a Fellow of [[Christ Church, Oxford]]. He married Hilda Weston Dott (1890–1986) in 1920. They had five children and thirteen grandchildren.<ref name="Chaundy"/>
